tier: standard           # additive spec-paths key follows 20260819/02 + 20260820/05 + 20260821/01 precedent; scope-reconcile.js (critical-named) gets one additive read-only flag, no behavioral edit to existing modes (pinned by AC-12); init runs only at bootstrap — worst failure is a broken bootstrap in a fresh host, recoverable by re-run

survivors.claim: A non-array profile.settings.extraAllow/extraDeny crashes generate with an unhandled TypeError at exit 1 (no remedy, no init-gen: prefix), outside the exit-4 boundary - the same 'settings-derived throw collides with a documented exit code' class round 2 was built to close, for a field its own array-shape sweep omitted.
survivors.impact: A malformed profile field the schema documents as an array crashes the bootstrap with a raw, unlabeled stack trace that looks exactly like a manifest-check failure, instead of a clean, remedy-bearing refusal.
survivors.evidence: Executed: node spec/scripts/init-gen.js generate --root <host> --profile <profile w/ settings.extraAllow: 5> -> TypeError: (p.settings.extraAllow || []) is not iterable at mergeSettings (spec/scripts/init-gen.js:505:93) ... Node.js v26.0.0 ... exit 1 (no init-gen: prefix, no remedy). Confirmed the throw site (505/513) runs at line 563, before the try block starts at line 570; a scratch mutant with the try/catch stripped confirmed the boundary works for the EISDIR case but does not cover this call site. Nothing is written on disk in this repro (no data loss).

survivors.claim: The unreadable-settings pre-flight remedy always says 'Fix the file's permissions (chmod u+r ...)' even when the read failure is EISDIR (settings.json is a directory), which chmod cannot fix.
survivors.impact: An operator whose settings.json got replaced by a directory is told to fix file permissions, which does not address the actual problem.
survivors.evidence: Executed: made .claude/settings.json a directory, ran generate -> 'init-gen: cannot read existing .../.claude/settings.json (EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read) ... Fix the file's permissions (e.g. chmod u+r ...) and re-run generate.' Exit code (2) and no-write guarantee are correct; only the remedy wording is mismatched to the cause.
